mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines evaporation?

options.A: Change of water from liquid to gas at its surface below its boiling point.
options.B: Change of water from solid directly to gas.
options.C: Change of water from gas to liquid.

mcqs.answer: Change of water from liquid to gas at its surface below its boiling point.
mcqs.explanation: Evaporation is the process where liquid water turns into water vapour from the surface at temperatures lower than the boiling point. Option B describes sublimation, C describes condensation, and D describes boiling, not evaporation.

mcqs.question: When you see water droplets forming on the outside of a cold glass of lemonade on a hot day, which process is occurring?
mcqs.explanation: The cold surface cools the surrounding water vapour, causing it to change from gas to liquid as droplets. This is condensation. Evaporation is the opposite, sublimation is solid‑to‑gas, and precipitation refers to rain or snow falling from clouds.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes water vapour present in the air?

options.A: It is visible as tiny droplets.
options.B: It is an invisible gas that can become visible when it cools.
options.C: It is the same as the liquid water you can see.
options.D: It only exists near bodies of water.

mcqs.answer: It is an invisible gas that can become visible when it cools.
mcqs.explanation: Water vapour is a colourless, invisible gas. When it cools to the dew point, it condenses into tiny droplets that become visible (e.g., fog or clouds). Options A and C confuse vapour with liquid water, and D is incorrect because water vapour is present everywhere in the atmosphere.

mcqs.learning_point: Factors affecting evaporation at an introductory level
mcqs.question: A shallow pan of water is left in direct sunlight on a windy day, while a covered pot of water sits on a cool night balcony. Which will evaporate faster?

options.A: The shallow pan in sunlight and wind.
options.B: The covered pot on the cool night balcony.
options.C: Both will evaporate at the same rate.

mcqs.answer: The shallow pan in sunlight and wind.
mcqs.explanation: Higher temperature, larger exposed surface area, and wind increase the rate of evaporation. The covered pot is cooler, has less surface area exposed, and lacks wind, so it evaporates much slower. Options C and D ignore these factors.

mcqs.learning_point: Examples of evaporation in daily life
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a common misconception about evaporation?

options.A: Evaporation can occur at any temperature.
options.B: Evaporation only happens when water boils.

mcqs.answer: Evaporation only happens when water boils.
mcqs.explanation: Many think evaporation needs boiling, but it occurs at all temperatures, especially at the surface. Option A is true, C is not required (still occurs without wind), and D is true because evaporation turns liquid into invisible vapour.

mcqs.learning_point: Examples of condensation in daily life
mcqs.question: Why does dew form on grass in the early morning?

options.A: Because grass releases water vapor into the air.
options.B: Because the temperature of the grass drops below the dew point, causing water vapour to condense.
options.C: Because wind pushes water droplets onto the grass.
options.D: Because sunlight heats the grass and creates droplets.

mcqs.answer: Because the temperature of the grass drops below the dew point, causing water vapour to condense.
mcqs.explanation: When the grass cools during the night, its surface temperature can fall below the dew point of the surrounding air, leading water vapour to change into liquid droplets (dew). Options A, C, and D describe incorrect mechanisms.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares evaporation and condensation?

options.A: Evaporation is the change from gas to liquid; condensation is the change from liquid to gas.
options.C: Evaporation absorbs heat from the surroundings, while condensation releases heat.
options.D: Condensation requires wind, whereas evaporation does not.

mcqs.answer: Evaporation absorbs heat from the surroundings, while condensation releases heat.
mcqs.explanation: Evaporation is an endothermic process (it takes heat), and condensation is exothermic (it gives off heat). Option A reverses the definitions, B is false because both occur at many temperatures, and D is not a defining requirement.

mcqs.question: In the water cycle, condensation is crucial because it: (i) releases latent heat, (ii) forms clouds, (iii) increases atmospheric pressure, (iv) converts water vapour directly into ice. Which combination is correct?
mcqs.explanation: Condensation releases latent heat (i) and leads to cloud formation (ii). It does not directly increase atmospheric pressure (that is a result of many processes) nor does it always convert vapour directly into ice; that specific transition is deposition, not ordinary condensation. Hence only statements i and ii are correct.
